strengths: Comprehensive quantification of sinusoidal representation universality across models and layers with multiple validation approaches (RSA, Fourier analysis), extending prior work with concrete evidence of convergence

Methodologically important finding that probes trained on natural language contexts generalize robustly across both natural and synthetic tasks, while synthetic probes fail on natural language—challenging prior assumptions and having direct practical implications
Well-designed param-sin probe that improves on prior work by explicitly parametrizing frequency, amplitude, and phase-shift; demonstrated to outperform baselines across diverse settings

Thorough cross-layer analysis elegantly demonstrating interchangeability of representations through single-layer and leave-one-out schemes, with strong evidence of consistent encoding throughout models
Mechanistic intervention experiments (steering toward sinusoidal patterns) provide causal evidence linking representation structure to arithmetic accuracy
Effective demonstration of why general-purpose interpretability tools are inadequate for specialized data types, motivating need for tailored approaches
Solid technical execution with appropriate evaluation methodologies (RSA, Fourier analysis, linear probing, mechanistic interventions) providing triangulation of claims
weaknesses: Generalizability claims substantially overstated given limited model scope: only 3 families, maximum 15B parameters (explicitly excluding >30B), single language (English), no proprietary models tested, and Phi family showing notably weaker alignment; claim of 'almost perfect universality' not fully supported

Complete absence of multilingual or cross-linguistic-system evaluation despite acknowledging this limitation; no exploration of how findings generalize to non-English number systems (Chinese, Japanese, etc.)

Mechanistic evidence is indirect and overstated: steering corrects only 30-42% of errors, Table 2 shows 56.8% of subtraction errors have internally correct results but wrong output (indicating sinusoidality is one of multiple factors), and claims about sinusoidality 'determining' accuracy conflate correlation with causation

Critical multi-token number finding (accuracy drops to near-zero after position -1) raises severe concerns about practical applicability for real numbers but lacks deep analysis of why this occurs or how to address it

Ordinal data section (4.3) underdeveloped: uses leave-one-out on tiny datasets (7 days, 12 months), inconsistent results with older probe sometimes outperforming new approach, and acknowledged probe blind spot with zero values unresolved

Limited arithmetic scope with concerning results (division at only 5.9% accuracy in Figure 7) inadequately analyzed; no exploration of why operations differ so dramatically or investigation of complex mathematical operations

Probing interpretation gaps: linear decodability doesn't necessarily reflect true representation structure, and the inference that lower probing error indicates sinusoidality could be questioned; missing validation that probed structure is causal

Statistical rigor lacking: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars; sensitivity analysis missing for key hyperparameters (e.g., k=63 Fourier cutoff); strong claims based on point estimates
Natural language context findings under-explored: shows robustness (Figure 4) but doesn't analyze why; missing ablation studies to isolate key factors and sensitivity analysis for dataset dependence

Technical novelty is incremental: param-sin improves over prior sin probe but represents modest architectural adjustment rather than fundamental methodological advance; empirical findings extend prior work rather than introducing novel principles

strengths: Comprehensive empirical analysis across 8 models, multiple sizes, and diverse contexts with natural language evaluation that extends beyond prior synthetic-context work
Methodological contribution: the param-sin probe (Eq. 2) is a genuine improvement with better regularization and stricter sinusoidal constraints
Valuable finding that natural-language-trained probes generalize across contexts while synthetic-trained probes fail, with important implications for interpretability methodology
Multiple convergent analytical approaches (RSA, Fourier decomposition, IoU metrics, cross-layer generalization) strengthen claims about representational consistency
Direct mechanistic evidence via steering experiments linking sinusoidality to arithmetic accuracy (Section 4.2, Figure 9)
Full code release and detailed experimental specifications support reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core findings about sinusoidal representations come from prior work (Kadlcík et al. 2025, Zhou et al. 2024, Kantamneni & Tegmark 2025); this paper mainly consolidates with marginal improvements to the probe architecture
Overstated 'universality' claims: Phi models show weaker alignment (Figure 1), first/last layers significantly underperform (Section A.6), and k=63 for IoU appears post-hoc selected from Figure 10

Critical limitations not adequately highlighted: multi-token numbers drop to near 0% accuracy for 5+ tokens (Figure 6), and division accuracy remains only 5.9% (Figure 7), undermining claims about universal numeric representations
Shallow mechanistic insights despite 'mechanistic' framing: paper shows sinusoidality correlates with accuracy but doesn't explain why this representation emerges or why alternatives aren't used
Modest practical improvements: error reduction via steering is 30-42%, layer removal strategy is admittedly 'extremely naive', and applicability is unclear
Limited model and language scope: excludes >30B models, English-centric only (with unaddressed implications for myriad-based number systems), only 3 model families tested, risking rapid obsolescence
Ordinal data analysis underdeveloped: Table 1 uses only 6-12 examples with high variance, leave-one-out evaluation on 7 days is unconvincing, reads as appendix-quality work
No statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, significance testing, or hyperparameter sensitivity analysis across single runs; insufficient for empirical claims
Key insights relegated to appendices: residual stream explanation (A.7) and probe sparsity analysis (A.6) should be in main text; first/last layer discrepancy remains unresolved theoretically
Sensationalized framing: title 'Here's Why You Should Care' is informal for ACL; claims like 'strikingly systematic' and 'almost perfectly universal' overstate findings given observed variations

strengths: Rigorous experimental methodology with proper experimental design, multiple complementary analyses (RSA, Fourier, probing), and clear quantitative metrics for universality across multiple model families and sizes

Novel analysis in natural language contexts showing that probes trained on natural language generalize robustly across both math and natural language evaluation, while synthetic probes fail—an important practical finding

Strong mechanistic insights including multi-token superpositioning mechanisms (99% accuracy), activation steering with direct evidence linking sinusoidality to task accuracy, and identification of error-causing layers
Improved sinusoidal probe architecture (fparam-sin) that strictly constrains representations and consistently outperforms prior work and general-purpose tools like TunedLens
Excellent presentation with clear writing, effective visualizations, comprehensive appendix, honest limitations discussion, and commitment to reproducibility through code release
Generalization of findings to ordinal data types, suggesting broader applicability beyond pure numbers
weaknesses: Incremental novelty relative to recent prior work: sinusoidal structures were established by Nanda et al. (2023) and especially Kadlcík et al. (2025); fparam-sin is a minor architectural improvement; main contributions are quantifying universality and extending to natural language—meaningful but somewhat incremental

Significant scope limitations restrict generalizability: only three model families, maximum 15B parameters (excluding recent very large models), English-centric analysis with acknowledged uncertainty about multilingual LLMs with different number systems, potentially not representative of evolving frontier models

Severe experimental limitations in ordinal data section (4.3): only 6-11 training examples for 7-12 category tasks with leave-one-out evaluation, leading to unreliable confidence in results (e.g., 3-4/6 matches); small-sample effects not quantified
Multi-token number results plateau quickly: accuracy drops to near-zero beyond 3 tokens; mechanism of failure not thoroughly analyzed; limits practical applicability to numbers ≥10^9

Mechanistic evidence incomplete: activation steering improvements modest (up to 30-42% error reduction), lacking ablations on which sinusoidality components matter most, unclear if other parametrizations could be equally viable
Natural language context insights underdeveloped: Figure 4 shows expected domain adaptation effects but lacks deep analysis of why natural language helps or actionable guidance for probe design
Absence of statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or variance quantification; unreliable assessment of reliability on small-sample results

Limited practical implications: main takeaway is to use sinusoidal probes for interpretability, but unclear what practitioners should do with these insights or how to improve models; steering improvements don't solve arithmetic problems

Questions about causality: demonstrates correlation and intervention effects but unclear if sinusoidality is necessary or other representations could work equally well; universality might reflect shared optimization objectives rather than fundamental bias
Arbitrary methodological choices: k=63 selection is post-hoc; crossover point at k≈250 where random pieces have better agreement complicates universality claims
